sentences.text: 4.1. The appellants, being aggrieved and dis-satisfied with the order passed by the Reference Court dated 11.02.2019 in Land Reference Case Nos.126 of 2014 to 150 of 2014 (main LAR Case No.130 of 2014) have preferred this appeal.

entities.text: Land Reference Case Nos.126 of 2014 to 150 of 2014
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 4.2. Reference Court enhanced the compensation from Rs.5.5/- per Square Meter to Rs.330/- per Square Meter by awarding additional amount of Rs.324.50/- per Square Meter with additional compensation under Section 23(1)(a) and 12% increase per annum on the market value from the date of notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act') till the date of award of the Land Acquisition Officer to the date of award of the Collector or the date of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2924/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/07/2023 undefined taking possession of the land whichever is earlier.
Additionally, interest under Section 28 of the Act was also awarded.

4.3. A proposal of acquiring the land situated at Village:Itola, Taluka and District: Vadodara for the public purpose i.e. Dabka-Vadu-Bhoj-Sarasvani-Thikari-Itola Road was made and accordingly, a notification under Section 4 of the Act was published on 21.02.2002 and notification under Section 6 of the Act was published on 13.03.2003.
4.4. The award under Section 11 of the Act was passed on 31.07.2004 awarding an amount of Rs.5.5/- per Square Meter for irrigated land towards compensation for acquisition of the land in question.

4.5. The claimants being aggrieved by the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2924/2023 ORDER DATED:
14/07/2023 undefined order passed under Section 11 of the Act preferred reference as per Section 18 of the Act. This First Appeal pertains to the LAR No.126 of 2014 pertaining to Block Survey No.464 acquiring the area of 1560 Squre Meters.

The Reference Court awarded additional amount of Rs.8,04,889.80/- comprising of additional amount of Rs.5,06,220/- at Rs.324.50/- per Square Meter, Rs.1,51,866/- at 30% Solitium, and increase at the rate of 12% from 21.02.2002 to 31.07.2004 i.e. 29 months amounting to Rs.1,46,803.80/-.

5.1. Learned advocate Mr.K.M.Sheth for the respondents-claimants submitted that the Reference Court by judgment and award passed in LAR Nos.122/2014 to 125/2014 pertaining to the village:Itola for the very same purpose has awarded additional amount higher than the amount which is awarded in the impugned NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2924/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/07/2023 undefined judgment and award.

5.2. Learned advocate Mr.K.M.Sheth for the respondents referred to and relied upon the communication of the Section Officer, Road and Building Department to the Executive Engineer,
Panchayat Department, Vadodara dated 06.12.2021 whereby, it is stated that the State Government has accepted the judgment and award of LAR Nos.122/2014 to 125/2014 without treating the same as a precedent.

It was therefore submitted that as the appellant having accepted the judgment and order insofar as the LAR Nos.122/2014 to 125/2014, than the appeal is not required to be entertained as there cannot be any discrimination between the similarly situated land acquired for the very same purpose.

5.3. Learned advocate Mr.K.M.Sheth for the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2924/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/07/2023 undefined respondents also invited the attention of this Court to the judgment and order dated 27.04.2023 passed in First Appeal No.1714 of 2023 and other allied matters by the Special Land Acquisition Officer vs L H Of Decd. sentences.text:
Co- ordinate Bench of this Court (Coram: Hon'ble Mr.Justice Nikhil S. Kariel) arising out of the impugned common judgment and award rendered in LAR Nos.126/2014 to 150/2014 wherein,
considering the above facts, the appeals filed by the State Government were not entertained by observing as under :
"6.

Considering the submissions made by learned advocate Mr. Sheth for the respondents, this Court had called upon learned Assistant Government Pleaders appearing in respective appeals to take instruction and whereas, learned AGPs, upon instruction of one Mr. N.M.Naikawala, Executive Engineer, Panchayat Road and Building Division, Vadodara have confirmed that the judgment in LAR Nos.
122/2014 to 125/2014 have been accepted and whereas, the amount additionally awarded and deposited with the learned Reference Court had already been disbursed in favour of the claimants.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2924/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/07/2023 undefined 6.1.

In this view of the matter, more particularly, since it clearly appears that two sets of persons, whose lands have been acquired, more particularly, there being absolute similarity between the persons i.e. the claimants, could the Government be permitted to agitate the present group of appeals, more particularly, when the State had accepted the judgment of the LAR No. 122/2014 and allied matters.
In the considered opinion of this Court, the answer being an emphatic no, more particularly, even the Hon'ble Apex Court also having stated as much in a recent decision.

6.2. The Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Shivappa vs. The Chief Engineer and Others [Civil Appeal Nos. 2694- 2700/2023; order dated 11.04.2023] had inter alia observed that the State or its instrumentalities cannot be permitted to adopt an attitude of pick and choose and whereas, if the State had accepted the award of the Reference Court in respect of some of the claimants, it could not be permitted to adopt a different treatment to other claimants since such attitude smacks of patent discrimination.

entities.text: Shivappa vs. The Chief Engineer and Others [Civil Appeal Nos. 2694- 2700/2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Paragraph nos. 8, 9, 10 and 11 of the decision being relevant for the purpose, are quoted hereinbelow for the benefit:-
"8.

Another factor that needs to be taken into consideration is that the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2924/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/07/2023 undefined respondent-State itself had filed applications before the High Court for withdrawal of nine appeals arising out of acquisition under the same notification.
9. In the said case also, the Reference court had granted compensation at the rate of Rs. 4,61,250/- per acre.
The High Court, vide order dated 08.03.2016 has allowed the said appeal(s) to be withdrawn and the same had been placed on record before this Court in I.A. No. 59170 of 2016.

Though a period of more than six years had lapsed,
the said position is not contested by the respondents.

sentences.text: The State or its instrumentalities cannot be permitted to adopt an attitude of pick and choose.
11. If the State has accepted the award of the Reference Court in respect of some of the claimants, it cannot be permitted to adopt a different treatment to the other claimants.
Such an attitude smacks of patent discrimination."

7. Considering the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, more particularly, though in the present case, the issue is with regard to two separate groups of Land Reference Cases whereas since NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2924/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/07/2023 undefined it clearly appears that there is no discernible difference between the issues in both the Reference Cases, at the cost of repetition it being noted that lands belonging to the same village being acquired for the very same purpose, the Notification under Section 4 in both the cases issued near about the same time, there being a difference of approximately four months in Notification under Section 6 and whereas, the award of the Land Acquisition Officer of the very same day, there does not appear to be any difference between the lands involved in the present cases and the lands in case of LAR No.
122/2014 and allied matters.

7.1. It also appears, as noted hereinabove, that the highest claim in LAR No. 122/2014 and allied matters was to the tune of approximately Rs. Fifteen Lakhs i.e. Rs. 14,92,700/- to be precise whereas in the instant group of cases, the highest amount awarded was Rs. 12,33,100/-.

As stated by learned advocate for the respondents, it also appears that there are alteast seven cases in the present group where the additional amount awarded is even less than Rs. One Lakh and as mentioned hereinabove in LAR No. 128/2014 the additional amount came to Rs. 4,543/- only.
8.

In this view of the matter, in the considered opinion of this Court, there NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2924/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/07/2023 undefined does not seem to be any justifiable reason whatsoever for the State to have accepted the award in LAR Nos. 122- 125/2014 whereas, the present group of appeals concerning LAR Nos. 126- 150/2014 have been chosen for preferring of appeal.

9. In this view of the matter, more particularly, in light ofthe law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Shivappa (supra), in the considered opinion of this Court, the present First Appeals are not required to be entertained and are hereby dismissed in limini.
Consequently, the Civil Applications would also stand disposed of."
6. In view of the above observations made in the First Appeal No.1714 of 2023 and other allied matters, this Appeal is also not entertained and is ordered to be dismissed in limine.
Civil Application also stands disposed of as a consequence.

(BHARGAV D. KARIA, J) PALAK Special Land Acquisition Officer vs L H Of Decd. Chimanbhai Chaturbhai Patel on 14 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54686435/
